The reason this is unlikely to happen is because businesses, especially international ones, want to be able to trust tech companies with their data. Would you upload all your customer's data to the clouds I'd you knew that the data was insecure and easy to snoop on, not only by governments but by competitors, spammers, etc? Why do you think Microsoft fought the US govt tooth and nail to protect the data centers in Ireland which were subpoenaed? They're may have been some PR reasons and personal convictions of board members, but the main reason was because they wanted international businesses to trust their Azure platform.

This is bad for business. It's bad for consumers. It might be a marginal win for security if companies cave, though I suspect the main target for this is dark net markets, not terrorists.

Short of some highly litigated legislation, though, I can't see many businesses compromising their customer's security and their profits because the FBI asked nicely.
